gloss: to gaze at; to stare intently

definitions.gloss: to gaze at; to stare intently; to be transfixed by
definitions.explanation: To look at something so intently that one becomes absorbed in it. Implies fascination or deep interest rather than a blank stare. Compound of 見 (to look) + 入る (to enter), suggesting one's gaze enters deeply into the object.

examples.english: I gazed intently at the painting.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{水槽|すいそう}の{魚|さかな}に{見入|みい}っている。
examples.english: The children are staring intently at the fish in the tank.

examples.japanese: {夕焼|ゆうや}けの{美|うつく}しさに{思|おも}わず{見入|みい}ってしまった。
examples.english: I found myself involuntarily gazing at the beauty of the sunset.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
Godan verb (る ending, conjugates as r-row: {見入|みい}らない, {見入|みい}ります). Takes the particle に to mark the object being gazed at: ～に{見入|みい}る.

USAGE:
Often used with {思|おも}わず (involuntarily) to convey that the viewer was so captivated they couldn't help but stare. The nuance is always positive absorption, not hostile staring.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～に{見入|みい}る (to gaze at ~)
- {思|おも}わず{見入|みい}る (to involuntarily become absorbed in looking)
- じっと{見入|みい}る (to stare fixedly)
